skills_considered.reason: No study list arrived. The reading cursor was a single queue entry, FT-043, already deduplicated against the registries when PMID 30290271 created it; re-triaging one known record would add no disambiguation.
There is no batch to sweep. FT-043 was already an approved single-paper cursor with a stated reason, so a batch ranking could not change which source was opened.
Ranking one already-selected paper is vacuous, and no person-level prioritisation is permitted in the public edition.
The read subtracts an unsupported premise and documents a systemic confounder. It matures no therapeutic hypothesis; forging candidates on a correction would manufacture the appearance of progress.
The study administers no drug and tests no compound. There is no molecule to pass through the BLOCK-1 ADMET gate.
The paper concerns a mouse conditional allele generated by Cre-loxP. It carries no splice variant and no human allele for which a splice-switching oligonucleotide could be designed.
Corrections are isolated in a commit candidate. No BATCH_COMMIT was authorised in this session and the four scientific current files remain unchanged.

The source was read in full, sequentially, from a local fingerprinted artifact. A retrieval-augmented query over the corpus is a weaker evidence route than the reading already performed and would send text to an external API.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed exact-author counts measured 2026-08-06: senior/corresponding author Aldaz CM had 138 records, 38 of them WWOX; first author Ludes-Meyers JH had 13 records, 6 of them WWOX. This is the group that cloned WWOX (Bednarek 2000, reference 1 of this paper) and it is the originating laboratory for the Wwox-floxed allele, so its execution weight for WWOX mouse genetics is high and its provenance for this specific reagent is first-hand. It is an oncology laboratory, not a neurology or WWOX-DEE clinical group: the study design asks whether Wwox loss causes neoplasia, and the phenotyping is therefore oncological, haematological, metabolic and skeletal. That specialisation explains, but does not repair, the total absence of neurological assessment discussed under the locators.

queries.query: WWOX AND ("metabolic acidosis" OR "renal tubular acidosis")

field_density.note: The single most consequential density result: the query linking WWOX to metabolic or renal tubular acidosis returns exactly one record, and that record is this paper. The renal-tubular-acidosis hypothesis this paper advances for the cause of Wwox-null lethality has, in the seventeen years since, never been tested or even revisited by anyone including its authors. The same sparseness holds for hematopoiesis (3 records, one of which is this paper) and bone mineralization (1 record, this paper). By contrast WWOX-and-osteosarcoma returns 28. The field kept the oncological reading of the Wwox-null mouse and discarded the systemic-metabolic one, even though the systemic phenotype is what actually kills the animals and is the phenotype most likely to confound any brain measurement made in the same P14-P18 window.

multihop.note: All 28 references were read and all 28 PMIDs resolved. Twenty-two are WWOX-, model- or disease-direct and 22 of 28 occur somewhere in the structured state. The six absent are generic method or family-background sources (McCarrick DT-A positive-negative targeting 8364601, Lakso EIIA-Cre 8650183, Sun Fgf4 conditional 10802662, two SDR-family reviews 17234335 and 11847285) plus Krummel 11013073 on FRA16D characterisation, which is locus-direct but not load-bearing for any measured endpoint here. No new reading debt is opened by this paper, because the two references that matter most are already queued: reference 26 is PMID 19500159, already FT-042, and reference 27 is PMID 17803050, already FT-041. That is the decisive multi-hop result. The premise 'epileptogenesis in this model', which PMID 30290271 imports and attributes to this paper, is not measured here at all; it enters this paper only as a Discussion citation of references 26 and 27, which are rat lde papers. The premise chain therefore terminates in FT-042/FT-041, not here, and reading those two is now the only way to establish it as first-hand. Reference 17 is PMID 16223882, which carries a publication-integrity hold; it is cited once in the Introduction as one of four background xenograft examples and supports no measured result of this paper, so no claim derived from this reading depends on a held record.

corpus_crossquery.query: Which of the paper's 28 references already occur in the structured state, and what does the repository currently attribute to PMID 19936220 beyond what the paper measures?
corpus_crossquery.note: Mechanical audit after the vertical read. Horizontally, PMID 19936220 exists in the state only as the triage placeholder CORPUS P295 / LIT-0295, Tier B, status 'screened - corpus placeholder', with 'Claim links: none - triage only'. It is therefore cited nowhere as canonical support, which bounds the blast radius of the correction. Its load is entirely indirect and lives in prose: claim_registry_current CLAIM 005, working_model_current v4.0 changelog, the PMID 30290271 dossier and session evaluation, and discovery_ledger_current all state that 'early death and epileptogenesis' are imported premises from PMID 19936220 and Mallaret 2014. This reading confirms one half of that sentence and refutes the other. Early death is first-hand here and quantified. Epileptogenesis is not measured here in any form, and naming this paper as its source misattributes a rat citation to a mouse study. Those five surfaces need the attribution split, which is what the commit candidate proposes.

entries.proposition: Epileptogenesis is not measured anywhere in this paper. Its single appearance is a Discussion citation of a rat model, so the premise PMID 30290271 attributes to this study is second-hand here and terminates in references 26 and 27.
entries.snippet: Very recently a spontaneous mutation in the Wwox gene was identified in rats that showed severe growth retardation, experienced epileptic seizures and died without reaching maturity
entries.anchor: Discussion, seventh paragraph, citing reference 26 (Suzuki 2009, PMID 19500159). A post-reading mechanical audit of the body text confirms this is the only sentence in the paper containing the words seizure or epilepsy outside the reference list; the strings EEG, convulsion, hippocampus, GABA and behaviour do not occur at all.

entries.proposition: The rat lde allele that carries the seizure phenotype is a C-terminal frameshift, not a null, so its phenotype cannot be transferred to a Wwox-null mouse without an explicit allele-class argument.
entries.snippet: identified as a 13-bp deletion in Exon 9 of the Wwox gene resulting in a frame shift mutation causing aberrant amino acid sequences (371–424aa) at the C-terminal of the Wwox protein
entries.anchor: Discussion, seventh paragraph, immediately after the seizure sentence; different species, different allele class and, per reference 26's title, audiogenic rather than spontaneous seizures

entries.proposition: Early postnatal death IS measured first-hand here and is quantified, so that half of the imported premise is confirmed rather than refuted.
entries.snippet: As early as 72 h after birth 43% (15 of 35) of Wwox KOs had died and 77% had died by 17 days after birth and no mice survived past weaning
entries.anchor: Results, 'Cre-Recombinase Deletion ... Completely Ablates Wwox Expression', growth and mortality paragraph; cohort n = 35

entries.proposition: The knockout in this paper is produced by EIIA-Cre acting at the zygote stage, which is a different Cre driver from the BK5-Cre used by PMID 30290271, so this paper is the primary for the floxed allele but not for the importing study's exact knockout.
entries.snippet: The adenovirus EIIA promoter directs transcription of Cre-recombinase at the zygote stage of embryonic development resulting in deletion of floxed sequences in all cells of the developing embryo including the germ cells
entries.anchor: Results, second subsection, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: The EIIA-Cre driver is a defined commercial line, which makes the model-generation route reproducible and separately citable.
entries.snippet: were obtained from The Jackson Laboratory (Bar Harbor, ME; stock number: 003724)
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods, 'Generation of Wwox Knockout Mice Using EIIA-Cre Mediated Deletion'

entries.proposition: At postnatal day 18 the knockout is severely hypoglycaemic, a measured systemic state capable of altering brain marker expression and seizure threshold independently of any neuronal Wwox function.
entries.snippet: glucose levels of Wwox KO mice were significantly lower than wild-type and heterozygotes (63% of HET and 57% of WT levels
entries.anchor: Results, 'Wwox KO Mice Displayed Signs of Metabolic Acidosis and Kidney Failure', paragraph 1; Table 3 gives 143.50 mg/dL KO versus 250.6 WT, p = 0.000131

entries.proposition: The same animals are uraemic and acidotic, so the systemic confounder is not a single abnormal value but a documented multi-system metabolic crisis in the exact age window in which hippocampal phenotypes are reported.
entries.snippet: Wwox KO animals displayed blood chemistry values compatible with kidney failure since they showed higher blood urea nitrogen (BUN) (two-fold higher, p = 0.01). In addition, KO mice displayed dramatically reduced bicarbonate levels
entries.anchor: Results, 'Wwox KO Mice Displayed Signs of Metabolic Acidosis and Kidney Failure', paragraph 1

entries.proposition: The haematological arm of the systemic phenotype rests on two knockout animals, so leukopenia and anaemia are directionally documented but statistically thin.
entries.snippet: one of the two KO mice analyzed displayed 3% of nucleated red blood cells (NRBC)/100 WBCs, a clear sign of severe anemia, while none of the WT mice showed any NRBCs
entries.anchor: Results, 'Impaired Hematopoiesis and Splenic Athrophy', final paragraph; WBC n = 2 per genotype

entries.proposition: Heterozygous mice are phenotypically normal on every axis this study measured, which argues against Wwox haploinsufficiency in mouse and bears on how carrier genotypes are reasoned about.
entries.snippet: heterozygous mice did not show any abnormalities in postnatal growth and survival as well as blood or bone parameters highlighting that only one Wwox allele is sufficient for full function
entries.anchor: Discussion, bone paragraph, final sentence

entries.proposition: Nine knockout mice examined by four independent modalities showed no neoplasia, which directly contradicts the osteosarcoma phenotype reported for the other Wwox-null mouse.
entries.snippet: A total of nine 18d old Wwox KO mice were subjected to complete necropsies, X ray analyses and multiple organ histopathology. We did not observed any lesions compatible with neoplastic growth by any of the methodologies
entries.anchor: Results, final paragraph of 'Wwox is Required for Normal Bone Mineralization'

entries.proposition: The authors state the conflict with Aqeilan explicitly and leave it unresolved, so 'Wwox-null mice develop osteosarcoma' is a contested claim rather than a settled property of the genotype.
entries.snippet: we did not detect any lesions compatible with spontaneous osteosarcomas in any of the Wwox KO mice analyzed macroscopically, histopathologically and radiographically
entries.anchor: Discussion, penultimate paragraph, which reports Aqeilan's 4 of 13 (31%) periosteal lesions and closes with 'The reason(s) for the discrepancies between studies remain to be determined'

entries.proposition: The osteoid increase is a non-significant trend in the Results, reported at p = 0.07 with the hedging verb 'tended'.
entries.snippet: KO mice femurs tended to have more osteoid than WT and HET femurs (OV/BV %, 0.36% vs. 3.5%, p = 0.07)
entries.anchor: Results, 'Wwox is Required for Normal Bone Mineralization', paragraph 1. Note the internal transcription hazard: the numeric pair is ordered WT/HET first then KO, while the sentence subject is 'KO mice femurs', so 0.36% is the wild-type value and 3.5% the knockout one. The same inversion recurs for BV/TV and Md.V/TV in the preceding sentences.

entries.proposition: The Discussion restates that same p = 0.07 trend as an observed finding, an in-paper firming-up of a non-significant result that anyone importing the bone phenotype will inherit.
entries.snippet: We observed a decrease of bone formation in Wwox KO mice associated with a reduction of mineralization and concomitant increase in osteoid compared to WT and HET mice
entries.anchor: Discussion, bone paragraph, sentence 4; compare with the Results sentence quoted in the preceding locator

entries.proposition: The floxed allele retains a pgk-neo cassette in the 5-prime regulatory region and the authors explicitly tested that it is not a silent hypomorph, which is what makes Wwox-flox usable as a clean conditional reagent.
entries.snippet: allele containing the insertion of the ∼2 Kb neomycin resistance gene in the 5′ transcriptional control region of the Wwox gene had no detrimental affect on Wwox functions required for normal mouse growth, survival or reproduction
entries.anchor: Results, 'Generation of Mice with a Floxed-Wwox Allele', paragraph 2, following normal Mendelian ratios, litter size and postnatal development in flox/flox crosses

entries.proposition: The Mendelian-ratio test was performed at three days of age, inside the window in which 43 percent of knockout mortality has already occurred, so a passing chi-square here does not exclude perinatal loss.
entries.snippet: correct Mendelian ratios were obtained after genotyping 154 animals (p = 0.257 using the χ 2 -test)
entries.anchor: Results, second subsection, paragraph 2; Table 1 shows 30 knockout pups observed against 38.5 expected, an under-representation in the same direction as early mortality though not itself significant

entries.proposition: Growth failure is severe and quantified at postnatal day 14, establishing the wasting state that accompanies every other measurement in this paper.
entries.snippet: Wwox KO mice had a severe growth defect averaging only 4.2 g at postnatal day 14 compared to heterozygous and wild-type mice (6.82 and 7.07 g, respectively)
entries.anchor: Results, second subsection, growth paragraph

entries.proposition: The knockout brain is only marginally smaller in absolute terms while its share of body weight nearly doubles, which is the signature of brain sparing during wasting and must not be read as brain overgrowth.
entries.anchor: Table 2, Organ Weights, Brain row, n = 3 per genotype. Absolute brain weight falls 8.7 percent (0.390 to 0.356 g) while relative brain weight rises from 5.0 to 8.5 percent of body weight; the significant p-value attaches to the relative figure, which is driven by the denominator. This is the only brain measurement in the entire paper.

entries.proposition: Serum bicarbonate is reduced by a third in the knockout, the measurement on which the metabolic-acidosis interpretation rests.
entries.anchor: Table 3, Blood Chemistry Analysis, Total CO2 row; WT n = 3, HET n = 3, KO n = 4. The knockout standard error (±3.5) is ten times the wild-type one, so the group is both lower and far more variable.

entries.proposition: Complete ablation of Wwox protein is demonstrated by immunoblot in three peripheral tissues only. No brain lysate appears in the figure or anywhere in the paper, so this study does not establish Wwox absence in brain.
entries.snippet: Wwox protein expression is abolished in Wwox KO mice. Total protein extracts from the indicated tissues were analyzed by immunoblotting using Wwox specific antibodies
entries.anchor: Figure 2C image inspected at original resolution: exactly three Wwox/Actin immunoblot pairs, labelled Kidney, Lung and Spleen, each with WT, HET and KO lanes. Knockout lanes are blank and heterozygote lanes are visibly intermediate. The phrase 'a variety of tissues' in the Results resolves, in the figure, to these three. EIIA-Cre acts at the zygote stage so global deletion is expected, but expectation is not measurement.

entries.proposition: The targeting design places FRT sites around the neo cassette, making it FLP-excisable. This is a reagent property visible only in the figure and stated nowhere in the text.
entries.snippet: Insertion of the targeting vector into the Wwox allele introduced a new Bgl II (B) restriction site into Wwox Intron 1
entries.anchor: Figure 1A image inspected at original resolution: the panel key defines three symbols, Exon, loxP site and FRT site, and two FRT sites flank the Neo cassette in both the targeting vector and the conditional allele. FRT is never mentioned in the body text. Also recorded here: the published caption describes panels A, B and C while the image carries four panels A to D, and the Results text cites 'Figure 1C,D'.

entries.proposition: The knockout growth curve is flat from day 10 to day 17, which is growth arrest rather than slowed growth, and the plotted knockout animals are survivors of a cohort that was 77 percent dead by the final timepoint.
entries.snippet: F2 pups were weighed on postnatal days 3, 10, 14 and 17. 100% of Wwox KO mice died before weaning (21 days). WT, n = 18; HET, n = 43; KO, n = 8
entries.anchor: Figure 3B image inspected at original resolution: the knockout curve starts already below wild-type at day 3 (about 1.65 versus 2.35 g) and plateaus at about 4 g from day 10 to day 17 while wild-type and heterozygote rise linearly to about 7.7 g. Wild-type and heterozygote curves are superimposed throughout. Panel A shows the size difference in newborn littermates.

entries.proposition: Every bone parameter is significant on three knockout animals against five pooled wild-type and heterozygote animals, with knockout variance so wide that the effect size is poorly bounded, and the figure's significance threshold does not match the one the Results text reports.
entries.snippet: We did not observe differences between wild-type and heterozygous mice, therefore, we compared KO data (n = 3) with WT and HET data combined (WT+HET, n = 5)
entries.anchor: Figure 5C image inspected at original resolution: four bar charts (BV/TV, Md.V/TV, Tb.N, Tb.Th), each knockout bar carrying a single asterisk defined in the caption as *p<0.05, while the Results text reports p<0.01 for BV/TV and Md.V/TV. Knockout error bars on BV/TV and Tb.N span roughly half the bar height. Panel A microCT shows a markedly smaller distal femoral epiphysis in the knockout; panel B Von Kossa shows sparser black mineralised trabeculae.

entries.proposition: Wwox immunohistochemistry is shown for kidney only, in one animal per genotype, with the knockout section doubling as the antibody-specificity control.
entries.snippet: Kidneys from a WT (left panel) or a KO (right panel) 18 day old mouse were dissected, paraffin embedded and subjected to immunohistochemical staining using anti-WWOX antibody
entries.anchor: Figure 6 image inspected at original resolution: strong brown tubular staining throughout the wild-type panel against an essentially blank blue haematoxylin counterstain in the knockout, confirming antibody specificity on knockout tissue. Kidney is the only organ shown by immunohistochemistry, which supports the renal-tubular-acidosis hypothesis by expression localisation rather than by function.
